sources.entry: Hister - Personal web search engine with automatic indexing of visited websites. Supports offline local result previews, local files, multi-user handling and optional semantic search. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Hister is a self-hosted personal search engine that indexes the full text of pages you visit and local files, searchable from a web UI, terminal, or an MCP-connected AI assistant.
summary.what_it_does: Hister runs as a local or self-hosted server that stores and indexes the full contents of web pages and files you choose to keep. A Firefox or Chrome extension automatically saves newly visited pages to the server. Content can also be added by importing browser history and bookmarks, indexing local directories, importing files, or using a crawler to index websites. Search supports field filters, phrases, wildcards, negation, aliases, and result priorities. Optional semantic search uses an embeddings endpoint the user configures. Users can search through the browser, a TUI, the command line, or an AI assistant connected via MCP. Multi-user support keeps each user's documents and results separate on a shared server.
use_cases: personal full-text search of local files
import browser history and bookmarks into a searchable index
give an AI assistant access to my saved documents
shared personal search server for multiple users
how_to_run: Download the binary for your platform from the latest release and rename it to hister
On Linux or macOS, run chmod +x hister
Run ./hister listen (on Windows, .\hister.exe listen in PowerShell) and keep the terminal open
Install the Firefox or Chrome browser extension
Visit a page with the extension enabled, then search for a phrase from it in Hister
Alternative installs: Homebrew (brew install hister), Docker, or Nix
notable: Automatic indexing of pages visited through the browser extension
Local-first: no telemetry or mandatory cloud service
Web, terminal (TUI), command-line, and MCP AI-assistant clients
Optional semantic search via a user-configured embeddings endpoint
Multi-user support on a shared server
caveats: Server must be running to index pages and search them
Semantic search sends document text to whichever embeddings endpoint is configured
Development build requires Go 1.26, npm, and a C compiler for CGO dependencies
